items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: the way it sounds like a tenor sax imitating Dexter Gordon or something

ctx.x: I did have good ears, but I did not have a naturally great technique. I was slipping and sliding like everybody else. I did take piano lessons, thank God, with a wonderful lady in Summit, New Jersey, Miss Capitola Dickerson. And she was a fantastic – she was a jazz lover and she was a fantastic just person and teacher, and she told me stories about going to see Billy Taylor on 52nd Street, and she told me about – she’d play me her Art Tatum 78s. And I was a terrible pianist, period. But I loved her, and she just…

play in that language of Miles Davis or a Clifford Brown or a Charlie Parker on a French horn, that was – required a lot of work. But it was just like kind of slogging work which after a while you kind of get it. You just have to like get through the difficulties of the articulation of how am I going to get this note to go from here to there the way it sounds like a tenor sax imitating Dexter Gordon or something. How the hell am I going to do that? Sometimes you just play, play, play – and you get it.
Is that – I won’t even say easier – more possible to pull off by articulating each note more than slurring.
